anti_corruption_features: Ethernet FCS (CRC-32) on every frame — detects bit errors at the link layer.
Working Counter (WKC) per datagram — independent integrity check at the application layer; mismatch flags missing/misconfigured SubDevices.
Mailbox handshake on SM0/SM1 — atomic; partially-written messages never observed.
Process-Data Watchdog (PD WD) — silent-fail protection; forces Op → SafeOp on cyclic frame loss.
PDI Watchdog — local µC stall detection; drives outputs to Safe state.
SII checksum on EEPROM load — corrupt ESI prevents start-up.
anti_tampering_features: Register Write Enable / Write Protection (ESC reg 0x0020-0x002F) — selected registers can be hardware-locked against PDI or ECAT writes.
PDI Access bit (0x0501) — explicit ownership transfer of SII EEPROM between ECAT and PDI to prevent accidental concurrent access.
ESM state machine — illegal Op-state entry rejected; Op requires PreOp + SafeOp traversal.
confidentiality_features: Not specified — EtherCAT does NOT define encryption on the wire. Field-bus traffic is assumed to run in a physically protected environment.
EtherCAT traffic is typically air-gapped from corporate IP networks (via the Industrial DMZ pattern); cross-network bridging is achieved via EAP (EtherCAT Automation Protocol) at the plant level.
authentication_features: Not specified — EtherCAT does not define MainDevice authentication. Topology + Configured Station Address assignment is the implicit identity model.
Hot Connect groups define logical identity; MainDevice rejects unexpected Vendor ID / Product Code via ESI cross-check during start-up.
integrity_features_beyond_crc: Working Counter (WKC) — application-layer integrity per datagram.
fields.safety_features_fsoe: Safety over EtherCAT (FSoE, IEC 61784-3-12) is an optional black-channel-principle safety frame layered on the mailbox transport. FSoE adds: (a) end-to-end CRC + sequence number per safety frame, (b) watchdog timeout per safety connection, (c) FSoE Connection ID for end-to-end identity, (d) dual-channel architecture in safety end-points. The underlying EtherCAT network is NOT safety-rated; only the FSoE end-points are. FSoE achieves SIL 3 / Cat 4 / PL e for industrial functional safety.
future_security_pointers: Possible future addition of cryptographic message integrity at the EtherCAT layer (under discussion at ETG).
TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) coexistence may pull in IEEE 802.1AE (MACsec) for the shared TSN/EtherCAT segments.
Industry 4.0 + IoT bridges typically terminate trust at the EAP gateway and use OPC UA Secure Channel above for cross-plant authentication + confidentiality.
fields.notes: EtherCAT's threat model assumes the network operates in a physically protected industrial environment. Wire-level encryption / authentication is NOT in scope of the base spec. For applications that require it, FSoE provides safety integrity, and external IPsec / OPC UA / MACsec layers can be added at the network boundary.
